title: Streams, templates and exceptions
subtitle: Generic code that works for any type, input/output as flowing streams, and errors that jump to where they can be handled.

sections.title: Streams
sections.body: A stream is a sequence of characters flowing between a program and a device. cin (input), cout (output), cerr (errors). << inserts, >> extracts, and both chain. The stream classes form a hierarchy: ios → istream/ostream → ifstream/ofstream (files) and stringstream (strings).

sections.title: Formatting and file I/O
sections.body: Manipulators format output: setw(6) width, setprecision(2) with fixed, endl newline-and-flush. Files: ofstream f("a.txt"); f << 42; — the destructor closes it (RAII). Check if (!f) after opening.

sections.title: Function templates
sections.body: template <typename T> T maxOf(T a, T b) { return a > b ? a : b; } is a recipe; when you call maxOf(3, 9) the compiler instantiates a version with T = int, and maxOf(2.5, 1.5) another with T = double. One source, many type-specific functions, all checked at compile time with no run-time cost. The type must support the operations used (here >).

choices.text: At compile time, once per type used.

figures.caption: Figure 8.1.1 — instantiation
figures.note: The template is only a recipe until used.

sections.title: Class templates and the STL
sections.body: template <class T> class Stack { T data[100]; int top; … }; gives Stack<int>, Stack<string>. The Standard Template Library supplies containers (vector, list, map, set), iterators and algorithms (sort, find) all built from templates.

problems.answer: vector (contiguous memory); a list needs O(n) traversal.

sections.title: Exceptions: throw, try, catch
sections.body: When a function cannot continue, it throws an object. The runtime unwinds the call stack, destroying locals on the way, until it finds a matching catch. If none is found the program terminates. try { risky(); } catch (const runtime_error& e) { … }. Use exceptions for exceptional conditions, not ordinary control flow.

sections.title: Exception safety
sections.body: Acquire resources in objects whose destructors release them (RAII, smart pointers) and exceptions cannot leak. Catch by const&, order handlers from most specific to most general, catch (...) catches anything, and never throw from a destructor. Levels of guarantee: basic (no leak), strong (all-or-nothing), no-throw.

worked.why: Order catch blocks: derived exception types before their base.
catch (const base&) first would swallow every derived type, hiding the specific handlers.

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: Otherwise a base handler catches everything.
